arxiv-2112-03455.title: Hybrid guiding: A multi-resolution refinement approach for semantic segmentation of gigapixel histopathological images
arxiv-2112-03455.creator: André Pedersen, Erik Smistad, Tor V. Rise, Vibeke G. Dale, Henrik S. Pettersen, Tor-Arne S. Nordmo, David Bouget, Ingerid Reinertsen, Marit Valla
arxiv-2112-03455.description: Abstract Over the past decades, histopathological cancer diagnostics has become more complex, and the increasing number of biopsies is a challenge for most pathology laboratories. Thus, development of automatic methods for evaluation of histopathological cancer sections would be of value. In this study, we used 624 whole slide images (WSIs) of breast cancer from a Norwegian cohort.

arxiv-2206-03518.title: Models of Millimeter and Radio Emission from Interacting Supernovae
arxiv-2206-03518.creator: Nitika Yadlapalli, Vikram Ravi, Anna Y. Q. Ho
arxiv-2206-03518.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nitika Yadlapalli, Vikram Ravi, Anna Y. Q. Ho. This work utilizes established models of synchrotron-powered light curves for core-collapse supernovae in dense circumstellar environments, namely type IIn and Ibn, to demonstrate the potential for detecting millimeter emission from these events. The progenitor types of these supernovae are still an open question, but using the synchrotron light curves as probes for the circumstellar environments could shed light on the mass-loss histories of the progenitors and discern between different theories.

arxiv-2306-13402.title: Hypocoercivity for infinite-dimensional non-linear degenerate stochastic differential equations with multiplicative noise

arxiv-2501-05112.title: Unidirectional motion of topological defects mediating continuous rotation processes
arxiv-2501-05112.creator: Marisel Di Pietro Martínez, Luke Alexander Turnbull, Jeffrey Neethirajan, Max Birch, Simone Finizio, Jörg Raabe, Edouard Lesne, Anastasios Markou, María Vélez, Aurelio Hierro-Rodríguez, Marco Salvalaglio, Claire Donnelly
arxiv-2501-05112.description: Abstract Topological defects play a critical role across many fields, mediating phase transitions and macroscopic behaviors as they move through space. Their role as robust information carriers has also generated much attention. However, controlling their motion remains challenging, especially towards achieving motion along well-defined paths which typically require predefined structural patterning.

arxiv-2505-00779.title: Uncertainty-aware Latent Safety Filters for Avoiding Out-of-Distribution Failures
arxiv-2505-00779.creator: Junwon Seo, Kensuke Nakamura, Andrea Bajcsy
arxiv-2505-00779.description: Abstract Recent advances in generative world models have enabled classical safe control methods, such as Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability, to generalize to complex robotic systems operating directly from high-dimensional sensor observations. However, obtaining comprehensive coverage of all safety-critical scenarios during world model training is extremely challenging.

arxiv-2505-10943.title: Universal scaling of segment fluctuations in polymer and chromatin dynamics
arxiv-2505-10943.creator: Kirill E. Polovnikov 1 , 2 , {}^{1,2,\;}, Mehran Kardar 3 , {}^{3,\;}
arxiv-2505-10943.description: Abstract We demonstrate how center-of-mass (COM) motion influences polymer segment fluctuations. Cancellation of internal forces, together with spatially uncorrelated external noise, generally yields COM diffusivity scaling as 1 / s 1/s with segment length s s , regardless of fractal dimension, viscoelasticity, or activity.

pmc-10647219.title: The Role of Carbon in Metal–Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition-Grown MoS2 Films
pmc-10647219.creator: Tianyu Hou, Di Li, Yan Qu, Yufeng Hao, Yun Lai, Giovanni Sotgiu
pmc-10647219.description: Acquiring homogeneous and reproducible wafer-scale transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) films is crucial for modern electronics. Metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) offers a promising approach for scalable production and large-area integration. However, during MOCVD synthesis, extraneous carbon incorporation due to organosulfur precursor pyrolysis is a persistent concern, and the role of unintentional carbon incorporation remains elusive.

pmc-11324148.title: Perspectives and challenges in developing and implementing integrated dengue surveillance tools and technology in Thailand: a qualitative study
pmc-11324148.creator: Chawarat Rotejanaprasert, Peerawich Armatrmontree, Peerut Chienwichai, Richard J. Maude
pmc-11324148.description: BackgroundDengue remains a persistent public health concern, especially in tropical and sub-tropical countries like Thailand. The development and utilization of quantitative tools and information technology show significant promise for enhancing public health policy decisions in integrated dengue control. However, the effective implementation of these tools faces multifaceted challenges and barriers that are relatively underexplored.

pmc-11349817.title: Atypical presentation of polymicrobial cervicofacial necrotizing fasciitis: An extraordinary odontogenic infection in a healthy female patient
pmc-11349817.creator: Basel Khalil, Ibrahim Borghol, Akhilanand Chaurasia
pmc-11349817.description: Key Clinical MessageCervicofacial necrotizing fasciitis (CNF) can occur as a dental complication in young, healthy individuals. Early diagnosis, treatment, and awareness of severe acute cervicofacial pain, rapid swelling, and radiological gas formation are crucial. Broad molecular profiling is recommended for understanding the organisms involved in such infections in future research.

pmc-11437916.title: Is microfracture sufficient for high-tibial osteotomy, or should intra-articular hyaluronic acid and oral glucosamine-chondroitin be used as additional treatments?
pmc-11437916.creator: Ümit Aygün, Eyüp Şenocak, Mehmet Fatih Aksay, Ali Can Çiçek, Orkun Halaç, Serdar Toy
pmc-11437916.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the effects of microfracture (MF) versus intra-articular hyaluronic acid (HA) + oral glucosamine and chondroitin sulfate (GC) in addition to MF in patients with osteoarthritic knees who underwent medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy (MOWHTO) after an average follow-up of five years.

pmc-11482332.title: Dynamics of RNA localization to nuclear speckles are connected to splicing efficiency
pmc-11482332.creator: Jinjun Wu, Yu Xiao, Yunzheng Liu, Li Wen, Chuanyang Jin, Shun Liu, Sneha Paul, Chuan He, Oded Regev, Jingyi Fei
pmc-11482332.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Nuclear speckles are nuclear membraneless organelles in higher eukaryotic cells playing a vital role in gene expression. Using an in situ reverse transcription–based sequencing method, we study nuclear speckle–associated human transcripts. Our data indicate the existence of three gene groups whose transcripts demonstrate different speckle localization properties: stably enriched in nuclear speckles, transiently enriched in speckles at the pre–messenger RNA stage, and not enriched.

pmc-12590296.title: PARP Inhibitor Maintenance After First-Line Chemotherapy in Advanced-Stage Epithelial Ovarian Cancer
pmc-12590296.creator: Stamatios Petousis, Ilker Kahramanoglu, Christian Appenzeller-Herzog, Martina A. Angeles, Chrysoula Margioula-Siarkou, Joanna Kacperczyk-Bartnik, Esra Bilir, Christos Chatzakis, Giuseppe Caruso, Nicolò Bizzarri, Konstantinos Dinas, David D.L. Bowtell, Dale W. Garsed, Isabelle Ray-Coquard, Jonathan A
pmc-12590296.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the association of first-line poly(adenosine diphosphate-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARP inhibitor) maintenance therapy with efficacy and safety outcomes among patients with advanced-stage epithelial ovarian cancer. Introduction Advanced epithelial ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer (EOC) remains one of the most lethal malignant tumors, with little improvement in the 5-year survival rate over the past 3 decades.

pmc-12606438.title: Effectiveness of CRISPR-Cas in sensitizing bacterial populations with plasmid-encoded antimicrobial resistance
pmc-12606438.creator: Johannes Kippnich, Fabienne Benz, Hildegard Uecker, Franz Baumdicker
pmc-12606438.description: The spread of bacteria resistant to antibiotics poses a serious threat to human health. Genes that encode antibiotic resistance are often harbored on plasmids, extra-chromosomal DNA molecules found in bacteria. The emergence of multiresistance plasmids is particularly problematic and demands the development of new antibiotics and alternative strategies.

pmc-12729430.title: The Impact of Entrepreneurs’ AI Literacy on Entrepreneurial Resilience: The Role of AI Anxiety and Social Support
pmc-12729430.creator: Yirong Liu, Haiqing Hu, Weiwei Kong, Hua Pang
pmc-12729430.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In the contemporary entrepreneurial environment increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence, the Artificial intelligence (AI) literacy of entrepreneurs plays an essential role in enhancing entrepreneurial resilience. However, the underlying mechanisms that explain this relationship remain inadequately explored. Grounded in the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines the effect of entrepreneurs’ AI literacy on entrepreneurial resilience, specifically assessing the mediating effect of AI anxiety and the moderating effect of social support.

pmc-13146298.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A577 HIDDEN CAUSES IN LOBAR INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE: DIAGNOSTIC YIELD OF DELAYED INVESTIGATIONS IN INITIALLY CRYPTOGENIC CASES
pmc-13146298.creator: Antonio Cruz Culebras, Rocio Vera, Alicia De Felipe, M Consuelo Matute Lozano, Sebastian García Madrona, Ana Sánchez Asensio, Laura Gil Martinez, José Carlos Méndez, Jaime Masjuan
pmc-13146298.description: Background and aimsLobar intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is frequently associated with identifiable etiologies, including cerebral amyloid angiopathy, hypertension, anticoagulation, vascular malformations, or neoplastic disease. However, in a subset of patients no cause is identified. Data on the diagnostic yield of delayed investigations in lobar ICH of unknown origin are limited.

pmc-13263711.title: Navigating Hope and Illness Cognition in Advanced Ovarian Cancer Patients: A CSM‐Based Phenomenological Study
pmc-13263711.creator: Yun Long, Chunchang Zhong, Cuili Wen, Fang He, Yufen Wang, Cairong Wang, Hui Xia, Yunhuang Shi, Ping Jin
pmc-13263711.description: BackgroundAdvanced ovarian cancer patients face profound psychosocial challenges in maintaining hope amidst terminal illness and treatment uncertainty. Understanding mechanisms supporting adaptive hope could inform psychosocial interventions.MethodsPhenomenological qualitative study of 16 women with advanced ovarian cancer receiving platinum‐based and/or targeted therapies at a tertiary center in southern China.

pmc-13689214.title: The impact of pain neuroscience education on physical therapy students’ pain knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, and clinical recommendations: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13689214.creator: Ahmad Muhsen, Bodor Bin Sheeha
pmc-13689214.description: BackgroundPain neuroscience education (PNE) promotes a biopsychosocial understanding of pain among health-professional students, yet evidence for its long-term effects outside high-income countries remains limited. This study evaluated the immediate and six-month effects of a single PNE lecture on pain knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, and clinical recommendations in Jordanian physiotherapy students.
